subject.title: [Bug] v2026.6.9 QQBot: long markdown reply is split into N independent bubbles (one per chunk), not a single message

question: Should QQBot merge markdown chunks that fit under the safe byte limit into one visible message, or should it preserve the current proactive split-by-safe-limit behavior for all chunker output?
rationale: Current source and tests support proactive self-contained chunks, but the issue and linked PR show a real user-visible fragmentation problem for chunks that are already below the safe byte limit; automation should not choose that UX contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Land bounded safe-size merging
options.body: Accept the linked PR direction: merge chunks only when the joined payload remains within the QQBot safe byte limit and keep oversized replies on the existing split path.

options.title: Keep split-by-design behavior
options.body: Treat the current self-contained chunking policy as intentional, close this issue and associated merge PRs, and document why multiple bubbles are expected for long markdown.

options.title: Request more live transport proof
options.body: Ask for an additional live QQ run that covers both safe-size merges and oversized overflow before deciding the permanent delivery policy.

recommendation.title: Land bounded safe-size merging
recommendation.body: Accept the linked PR direction: merge chunks only when the joined payload remains within the QQBot safe byte limit and keep oversized replies on the existing split path.

likelyOwner.reason: sliverp authored the central chunker history and has already stated the current design rationale on this issue.
